title: Do Verifiers Reduce Security-Relevant Misconfigurations? A Preregistered Paired Evaluation of Verifier-in-the-Loop GVR for Intent-to-Configuration
abstract: We preregistered and executed a deterministic paired experiment to test whether embedding a reachability/policy verifier inside a generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces security-increasing (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations produced by an LLM-driven intent→configuration pipeline. Using Dockerized FRRouting-style emulation, two deterministic validators combined with a logical-OR scoring rule, and a matched sample of N = 300 intents (150 benign + 150 programmatic adversarial variants), we compared single-pass LLM generation (baseline) to an LLM+verifier GVR pipeline implemented under a frozen protocol (preregistration cnd-2026-netops-gvr-security-01-prereg-v1). The adapter used shared_initial_candidate semantics: one initial LLM candidate was generated per paired intent and the same candidate was replayed to both arms (baseline is therefore not an independent-generation condition). The run completed all planned episodes with model_calls_used = 300 (shared candidate). Confirmatory outcome: baseline_success = 300 and guarded_success = 300 (contingency n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0); validators never reported forbidden reachability and the repair step was never invoked. Paired risk-difference = 0.0, McNemar two-sided p = 1.0, 95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Observing 0/300 violations gives a one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound ≈ 0.00994 on an undetected baseline violation rate. Because the repair path was not exercised, this study quantifies that inserting a verifier does not change observed compliance when baseline generation already satisfies the safety predicate under the chosen contract; it does not provide evidence that verifier-guided repair can rescue genuine violations. We archive the preregistration, deterministic execution accounting, per-episode validator traces, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility and to guide follow-up stress tests designed to exercise the repair path.

sections.introduction: Automating intent-driven network configuration with large language models (LLMs) promises efficiency gains but raises operational security concerns: generated configurations can expand attack surface, violate access-control policies, or break availability guarantees. The systems and safety literature therefore recommends constrained generation, execution-oracles, and iterative generate–verify–repair (GVR) loops as mitigations. Yet rigorous, preregistered evidence assessing whether a verifier placed inside a GVR loop actually reduces security-relevant (forbidden-reachability) misconfigurations under adversarial inputs is limited. We address this gap with a preregistered paired experiment focused on a single, operationally meaningful estimand: the paired absolute difference in the proportion of intents yielding forbidden reachability (guarded − baseline). Our contributions are evidence-grounded: (1) a machine-readable preregistration fixing a paired N = 300 confirmatory design; (2) a deterministic Dockerized execution using two deterministic validators aggregated by logical OR and a shared_initial_candidate generation contract to conserve hosted-model calls; (3) full execution and analysis artifacts showing a degenerate confirmatory result (n11 = 300) with a descriptive Clopper–Pearson upper bound on the undetected baseline violation rate (≈0.00994); and (4) artifact-grounded operational recommendations and reproducibility materials to inform follow-up stress tests that intentionally exercise the repair path.
sections.related_work: Three strands of prior work motivated our design. First, generate–verify–repair and execution-guided repair systems (applied to code and Infrastructure-as-Code) demonstrate that verifier feedback can substantially improve correctness, but realized gains depend strongly on verifier power and the repair strategy (e.g., TerraFormer and other recent GVR systems). Second, surveys and NetOps system papers document recurring LLM failure modes—hallucination, domain mismatch, and calibration issues—and consistently recommend integrating validators, constrained generation, or human oversight to reduce operational risk. Third, emulation and testbed research shows that execution-based validation is feasible for controlled evaluation but cautions about external-validity gaps when results are ported to production devices or live traffic. Existing records rarely combine a preregistered paired evaluation, deterministic validators, and archived per-episode verifier traces specifically targeting forbidden-reachability predicates. Our study occupies that niche by fixing generation semantics, prioritizing deterministic accounting, and archiving per-episode validator judgments and provider-call audits for reproducible inference.
sections.methodology: Design summary and estimand: The preregistration specified a paired binary design with N = 300 matched intents (150 benign seeds + 150 programmatic adversarial variants). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (absolute difference in proportion of intents yielding forbidden reachability). Primary test: exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05) with bootstrap-percentile confidence intervals for the paired risk-difference. Sampling and determinism: tasks were generated deterministically from a synthetic NetOps generator; all orchestration and emulator seeds were fixed and archived to ensure deterministic replay. Execution contract and generation semantics: to limit hosted-model cost we used shared_initial_candidate semantics—one LLM generation per pair was produced and replayed to both conditions—yielding model_calls_used = 300 for 300 pairs rather than up to 600 if independent draws per arm had been used. Arms and intervention: baseline = replay of the shared initial candidate; guarded = same shared initial candidate passed to two deterministic validators (a containerized execution-style reachability validator and a lightweight static reachability analyzer) whose outputs were combined by logical OR. If any validator reported forbidden reachability on the initial candidate the preregistered repair policy allowed up to one repair LLM call per pair. Validators, scoring rule, and determinism: two deterministic validators were used and their judgments combined with logical OR (a violation if any validator reported forbidden reachability). All per-episode validator traces, final/initial configuration parses, repair_applied indicators, and provider-call accounting were recorded and archived. Analysis plan: confirmatory analysis used the registered executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 (McNemar exact two-sided) and bootstrap-percentile CIs with a prespecified seed; sensitivity checks treating technical failures as violations were prespecified (no technical failures occurred).
sections.results: Execution and accounting: The run completed planned_episode_count = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions) with completed = 600 and failed = 0. Provider-call auditing under the shared_initial_candidate contract recorded model_calls_used = 300 and no cross-condition cache reuse; deterministic reconciliation checks passed. Primary confirmatory outcome: every paired intent passed the forbidden-reachability predicate in both arms: baseline_success_count = 300 and guarded_success_count = 300. The paired contingency is n11 = 300, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (Table 1). The paired risk-difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. The prespecified paired bootstrap-percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) is [0.0, 0.0]. Descriptive bound on undetected baseline rate: observing 0 violations in N = 300 yields a one-sided Clopper–Pearson 95% upper bound on the baseline violation probability of 1 − 0.05^(1/300) ≈ 0.00994. Repair and validator activity: validators never reported forbidden reachability on any initial candidate, so no repair calls were invoked and all per-episode repair_applied flags are false. The two deterministic validators were concordant on every episode; representative per-episode traces and the full execution manifest are archived for inspection.
sections.discussion: Interpretation constrained by design: Under the exact adapter contract (shared_initial_candidate), declared model (gpt-5-mini), the evaluated deterministic validator set combined by logical OR, the emulator, and the programmatic adversarial perturbations used, baseline generation satisfied the forbidden-reachability predicate on every sampled intent; therefore inserting the verifier did not change observed compliance. This is a scientifically supported negative (degenerate) confirmatory outcome, not evidence that verifiers are unnecessary in general. Importantly, the preregistered repair path was never exercised, so this experiment provides no evidence about whether verifier-guided repair can rescue violating initial candidates. Statistical and design implications: the paired-test power calculation presupposed a nonzero baseline violation rate and a target 30 percentage-point absolute reduction; that assumption was violated by the observed contingency and renders the McNemar inference uninformative for repair efficacy. Methodological lessons for future stress tests: (1) generation semantics materially affect sensitivity—shared_initial_candidate reduces model-call overhead but also reduces between-arm variability and the chance of discordant pairs that repair could correct; independent-condition generation (two independent LLM draws per pair) or larger repair-call budgets would better exercise repair efficacy at the cost of additional hosted-model calls; (2) adversary potency matters—the programmatic adversarial variants used here did not trigger validator-detectable violations for the chosen model and validators, so follow-up stress tests should target adversary design specifically against the chosen verifier predicates; (3) verifier diversity and strength matter—evaluating more powerful or production-grade execution oracles and a broader set of verifier modalities increases the chance of detecting real violations; (4) reproducible deterministic accounting is practical and valuable—fixed seeds, containerized emulation, and archived per-episode validator traces permit exact auditing of observed contingencies and provider-call budget trade-offs. Operational implication: when baseline generation already satisfies the declared safety predicate under a frozen contract, inserting a verifier may confirm compliance without changing outputs; demonstrating repair efficacy requires experimental designs that increase the probability of initial violations (stronger adversaries, independent draws, or weaker verifier thresholds) so that repair paths can be exercised and measured. All artifacts needed to reproduce and extend these conclusions are archived.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, deterministic paired evaluation of a verifier-in-the-loop GVR pipeline for intent→configuration generation using a declared LLM (gpt-5-mini), two deterministic validators combined by logical OR, and shared_initial_candidate generation semantics. The run completed N = 300 matched pairs with model_calls_used = 300 and produced a degenerate outcome: both baseline and guarded arms passed the forbidden-reachability predicate on all pairs (n11 = 300). Because validators never reported violations, the repair path was not invoked and the experiment cannot evaluate whether verifier-guided repair rescues violating outputs. The study demonstrates that generation semantics, adversary design, repair budget, verifier strength, and model diversity control whether a verifier-in-the-loop architecture can be shown to reduce security-relevant misconfigurations. We release the preregistration, execution manifest, per-episode validator traces, raw responses, and analysis artifacts in an archived evidence bundle to enable reproducibility and to inform targeted follow-up stress tests that intentionally exercise repair paths.

limitations: Degenerate confirmatory outcome: zero discordant pairs (n11 = 300, n10 = n01 = n00 = 0) render McNemar inference uninformative about repair efficacy when baseline violation rates are nonzero; the preregistered power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline violation rate and targeted detecting a 30 percentage-point absolute reduction.

GVR not exercised: under the chosen task set, emulator, model, and validators the verifier never reported forbidden reachability and consequently the guarded repair step was never invoked; the experiment therefore tests whether verifier insertion changes compliance when baseline is already compliant, not whether verifier-guided repair rescues violations.

Generation contract choice: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced one LLM call per pair and reduced model-call overhead but also limited independent draws that could produce discordant errors; alternative contracts (independent-condition generation or expanded repair budgets) would better exercise repair paths.

Adversarial-perturbation detail: the preregistration specified programmatic generation of one adversarial variant per benign seed; per-task generation seeds and intent payloads are archived in the evidence bundle for reproducibility.

External validity: tasks were synthetically generated and executed in deterministic FRRouting-style emulation; results do not necessarily generalize to heterogeneous production devices, live traffic conditions, or different operational constraints.
Model and verifier scope: a single model (gpt-5-mini) and two deterministic validators were evaluated; other LLMs, stronger verifiers, or dynamic execution oracles may produce different outcomes.
